title: Dependency Negotiation Protocol and Commitment Telemetry
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Roadmap-level dependencies between Eng/Design/Security/Infra are often negotiated ad-hoc during planning, resulting in unclear commitments, repeated re-negotiation, missed gates, and last-minute escalations. Impact: increased delivery friction, missed dates, and opaque risk for PMs. Goal: Define a lightweight cross-team negotiation protocol (agreements, windows, and escalation) and instrument 'commitment telemetry' so ownership, agreement quality, and resolution velocity are measurable and visible on roadmap dashboards. The protocol must be simple to adopt (Linear fields + Slack workflow + Console dashboard) and support: (1) binding commitments for release gates, (2) conditional commitments (e.g., degrade-to variant), and (3) auto-escalation when negotiation window expires.
acceptance_criteria: Formal negotiation protocol doc published in Confluence with examples and templates
Linear custom fields created: "Commitment Type", "Commitment Window End", "Negotiation Owner", "Escalation Level"
Console dashboard shows top-10 active dependencies with time-in-negotiation, percent accepted, and open escalations
Pilot run with three cross-functional initiatives (Serving Runtime, Console, Private Deployments) and documented feedback
Playbook for automated reminders and escalation (Slack/Email) implemented and tested

decisions: Negotation windows standardized: 10 business days for high-impact infra/runtime, 3 business days for UX/polish
Escalation path: Negotiation Owner -> Initiative PM -> Product Leadership (if unresolved after escalation TTL)
Telemetry model: emit events to observability pipeline (commitment.created/changed/escalated/resolved) with minimal payload (issue_key, commitment_type, owner, window_end, escalation_level)
